First Steps

KITCHEN NOTES / BUILD FLAVOR

The garlic timeline

Garlic cooks quickly and burns even faster. It needs gentle heat and attention, not a screaming hot pan.

Gentle heat → Fragrant → Stop
Go to the technique ↓

THE SMALL DETAILS THAT HELP

Here's how.

  1. 01

    Start with warm oil

    Drop your chopped or sliced garlic into oil that is warm, not smoking hot.

    Look for You want a gentle, steady sizzle, not an aggressive pop and crackle.

  2. 02

    Watch the color closely

    Stir the garlic continuously. You are looking for it to become pale golden and fragrant, which takes about 30 to 60 seconds.

    Look for Do not walk away. Garlic can go from perfect to burnt in ten seconds.

  3. 03

    Stop the cooking

    The moment it smells amazing and is lightly golden, immediately add the next wet ingredient (like beans, broth, or tomatoes).

    Look for The liquid drops the temperature of the pan instantly, stopping the garlic from browning further.

A note worth keeping

Know what to look for.

Your kitchen smells intensely of savory garlic, and the pieces are pale blond, not dark brown.

Try it in a recipe ↓

AVOID THIS

Throwing garlic into a very hot pan at the same time as onions.

Onions take 5-10 minutes. Garlic takes 1 minute. If they go in together on high heat, the garlic will burn and turn bitter.

TRY THIS INSTEAD

Cook onions first, then add garlic for the last minute, or use gentle heat.

MAKE SUBSTITUTIONS

Keep the job. Expect a change.

If you are using garlic powder instead of fresh, it goes in with the dry spices, not sizzling in the oil on its own.

What if it burned?

If your garlic turns dark brown or black, throw it out, wipe the pan, and start over. Burnt garlic will make the entire dish taste unpleasantly bitter, and no amount of seasoning will fix it.
